To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photoperiod-induced changes in gonadal activity and prolactin levels in goats are mediated through the melatonin receptor located in the superior cervical ganglion of the brain.

the photoperiod response of gonadal activity and prolactin release to long days in goats is mediated via a melatonin-induced change in the sensitivity of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis to the inhibitory effects of long days.

(1) the photoperiod-induced increase in prolactine secretion and the suppression of gonad function are abolished or weakened in the absence of a diurnal change in plasma melatonin concentrations, (2) these changes in prolactin levels and gonadal function are induced by long days, and (3) these results suggest that the diurnal pattern of melatonin concentrations is necessary to induce photoperiodic responses in the goat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photoperiod-induced changes of prolactin secretion and gonadal function in goats.
understanding the mechanism by which photoperiod regulates the seasonal changes of gonadal function, and prolactin and melatonin secretion.
the role of the pineal gland in the control of seasonal changes in gonadotrophin and prolactin concentrations and the mechanisms by which the photoperiod is perceived by the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melatonin is not a hormone but a chemical that acts as a hormone in the presence of a specific target tissue and that the target tissue is the pineal gland.

the superior cervical ganglionectomy in female goats prevents the photoperiodically induced gonadal regression and increase in plasma prolactin concentration, and the abolition of the melatonin secretion pattern abolishes the photoperiod-induced changes in gonadal activity and prolactin concentration.

the pattern of the melatonin secretion under natural photoperiodic conditions is important for the regulation of seasonal changes in gonadotrophic secretion, gonadal function and plasma prolactin concentration in goats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
melatonin is necessary to induce photoperiodic responses of the gonads and prolactin in goats.
the photoperiod is the environmental signal that regulates the seasonal change in reproductive activity and that melatonin is the endogenous mediator of this effect.

the pattern of the secretion of melatonin is necessary to induce photoperiodic changes in gonadal activity and prolactin release, and that melatonin mediates the effects of long days in regulating seasonal changes in the gonadal axis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we found that the superior cervical ganglionectomy, which abolishes the daily change in melatonin levels, prevents the increase in prolaction secretion induced by long day length exposure and also prevents the gonadal regression induced by the same photoperiodic stimulus.
we have shown the role of melatonin in the photoperiod regulation of reproduction.
the pattern of secretion of the pineal hormone melatonin is important to the regulation of reproductive activity and prolactin release.
